ana: Heads up — after kernel-autoselect landed on canary, 8xA100 1F1B runs show intermittent 99th spikes (~20–50ms extra) and PP bubble stretches. Attaching small profiler snippet below.

ana: ```
timeline: step 100..112
  compute: ||||||||||||||||      ||||||||||||||||
  allreduce:     -----(ALLREDUCE)--------
  kv-cache:           miss x3 at steps 104,108
p99 increase corresponds to allreduce overlapping compute more often when kernel fallback occurs.
```

kevin: Can you paste the runtime.trace or perf_profile.json? also which kernel names are selected for matmul/softmax?

ana: pasted small excerpt: kernel selected=matmul_fp16_fast_q8 at step 102, then fallback to matmul_fp16_fallback at 105. softmax path stayed on fast. KV cache miss rate jumps ~3x during fallback windows.

matt: Hmm. That timing smells like the batching heuristic merged a microbatch that changed packing layout. If the matmul kernel relies on a particular pack (q8) it might not be valid after the merge -> fallback. Fallback causes longer kernel time which moves allreduce start into next microstep -> PP bubble stretches.

sara: Quick experiments to try: disable kv-prefetch, try microbatch=2 (we usually run 1), and force kernel-policy=legacy to see if stability improves.

sara: example run:
```bash
./run_bench --gpus 8 --pp 8 --microbatch 2 --kernel-policy legacy --kv-prefetch off 
```

infra-bot: deploy: runtime-canary v1.3.9 (kernel-autoselect) rolled to canary-cluster-3 at 2134567800. Use `runtime.rollback canary v1.3.8` to revert.

kevin: I'll capture NCCL traces + nvtx. Also want `nvprof --profile-from-start off` and collect `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for the same run. We should check if allreduce size crosses the tree/ring threshold and triggers a different algorithm.

ana: Opening perf regression issue #4521 with my raw traces and a csv sweep plan. I'll start a 12-hour parameter sweep: microbatch in [1,2,4], kernel-policy in [auto,legacy,quant_affine], kv-prefetch in [on,off].

matt: If this reproduces, we should consider altering batching heuristic to prefer pack-aligned merges (i.e., avoid merging microbatches that change tile dims used by the fast matmul kernel). A cheaper mitigation is to bias kernel-autoselect toward stability during 1F1B schedules.

sara: :thumbsup: also add an A/B test on dedicated nodes to measure p50/p95/p99 separately — hosted noise can mask this.

kevin: quick note — NCCL shows repeated small allreduces (2–4KB) that got aggregated into a larger tree case after kernel slowdown. I suspect compute stall -> comm coalescing -> algorithm switch. I'll upload nccl_trace and nvprof.

ana: thanks — will post the sweep results csv and a short flamegraph. For now rolling candidate to fallback policy on canary and scheduling the microbatch=2 run.

matt: TL;DR actionable:
- repro matrix (microbatch/kernel-policy/kv-prefetch) queued
- capture NCCL + nvtx + runtime.trace for each run
- experiment: force kernel-policy=legacy to confirm mitigation
- if confirmed, change batching heuristic to avoid pack-unfriendly merges or make kernel-autoselect prefer stable kernel under 1F1B

sara: Good plan. Keep ops folks in the loop if we need a quick rollback.

ana: will update issue #4521 with initial numbers by EOD. Thanks all. :coffee:
